sentences.text: Shri S.S. Kushwah, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Praveen Newaskar, learned Govt. Advocate for the respondents/State.

This intra court appeal challenges the final order dated 18/04/2017 passed in W.P. No. 2460/2017,
by which the writ court has dismissed the writ petition on the ground that mere show cause notice is assailed and the appellant can always approach the authority by filing appropriate response.

The respondent has issued show cause notice (Annexure P/1) to the appellant, by which he is required to explain by producing relevant documents that unaccounted articles found in his godown are being used for adulteration in food article or not under the Food, Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (for brevity, 'Act').
The grievance and apprehension of the appellant is that none of the articles mentioned in the impugned show cause notice falls within the definition of "food" as defined in section 3(j) of the Act and, therefore, no action can be taken by the authority under the Act against the appellant.
Be that as it may, we would not like to enter into the merit of the matter as the grievance of the appellant is merely against show cause notice where the petitioner can always approach the authority by showing cause and justifying possession of the articles mentioned in the impugned show cause notice.

Accordingly, the present writ appeal stands disposed of without disturbing the order passed by the writ court with observation that if the appellant submits written explanation accounting for the articles mentioned in the show cause notice dated 07/04/2017 then the competent authority i.e.
respondent No. 3 shall consider the same as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law.

Needless to emphasis that if the articles mentioned in the impugned show cause notice are found to be not capable of being used for adulteration in food articles under the Act then consequential action of withdrawal of impugned show cause notice be taken.
It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merit of the case and the competent authority is free to take appropriate decision as per law.
